result.title: Native Probability Outputs for Clinical Triage: An Evaluation of Calibration and Decision Accuracy
result.summary: Patient-facing triage requires an appropriate care recommendation and recognition of when information is insufficient. We evaluate whether Jev, a decision model that returns probabilities over predefined actions, supports both judgments. Using CARE-Bench, we compare Jev with four general-purpose language models and three input-independent baselines across 925 decision points from 439 public cases. On the public test subset, Jev ranks fourth of five models by macro-F1 (0.461) but has the lowest observed multiclass Brier score (0.610), an 18.7\% improvement over uniform prediction (case-bootstrap 95\% interval, 4.9--31.1\%). Noul has lower binary Brier than Choice (0.215 versus 0.276). A evaluation of 453 HealthBench conversations again gives Jev the lowest observed Brier score (0.299), but measures a distinct emergency-referral judgment. Jev combines lower probability error with missed clarification needs in the four-action task. Asking about information sufficiency separately increases recall but also produces frequent unnecessary clarification assignments.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究在临床分诊场景中评估返回动作概率的决策模型 Jev，用 CARE-Bench 与通用语言模型及无输入基线对比，考察概率校准（Brier）与「信息是否充分」的识别能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 领域远离视觉，但「信息不足时是否需追问」与概率校准评价，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策收益/成本及停止置信度评价提供参照，可供核查。
